chunks: Examples of operating systems. The question: Name some operating systems.
Operating systems come in groups. Desktop and phone systems include Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS. Embedded devices with a bigger processor often run embedded Linux.
Small microcontrollers run a real-time OS (RTOS), such as FreeRTOS or Zephyr. Which one fits depends on the hardware and on how strict the timing and safety needs are.
Think of vehicles. A bicycle, a car and a freight truck are all vehicles, but you pick one by the load and the road.
A tiny microcontroller with a few kilobytes of RAM is a bicycle job, so you want a very light OS.
A device with a screen, Wi-Fi and megabytes of RAM can carry a heavy one like Linux. Using a truck for a bicycle job just wastes resources.
A first-cut decision path. Real choices also weigh licence, vendor SDK support (many chip vendors ship FreeRTOS or Zephyr by default), certification evidence and team experience.
RTOS: ("What a real-time operating system is"): a small OS whose timing is predictable and bounded.
Embedded Linux: the Linux kernel plus a minimal set of programs, customized for one device. MMU: hardware that gives each program its own private view of memory.
Standard Linux needs it. FreeRTOS / Zephyr: two popular open-source RTOSes for microcontrollers.
A small chip with 32 KB of RAM reads a sensor and sends the data over Bluetooth. That is a job for FreeRTOS or Zephyr, because Linux will not fit.
Now take a device with a display and Wi-Fi, built on a processor with an MMU and megabytes of RAM. That suits embedded Linux, which brings drivers and networking.
A product that needs safety certification, such as in a car or aircraft, may choose a commercial RTOS such as VxWorks or QNX. That is the whole idea.
"Three families. General-purpose: Windows, macOS, Linux; mobile: Android and iOS. Embedded Linux, built with Yocto or Buildroot, for application-class processors with an MMU.
And RTOSes for microcontrollers: FreeRTOS, Zephyr, ThreadX, VxWorks, QNX, µC/OS, RTEMS.
I'd pick by hardware and requirements: FreeRTOS or Zephyr on small Cortex-M parts, Linux on Cortex-A devices, a certified commercial RTOS where safety standards apply."
